answer: Cheap identities are the whole attack, so the defence is making every claim cost real work. The hollow of each epoch is a paid set of verifiable contributions, which makes farming accounts expensive and noisy. A pearl of per-task receipts records who did what, and the canyon of that record is inspected by auditors who gain nothing from passing it. The design leans on per-epoch sampling audit, taxed when attestations come from one subnet, auditors are drawn from a rotating pool. Written in a numbers heavy, no adjectives register, it stays short.
